items.followUp: Define valency and state the valency of oxygen.

rubric.description: Defines valency as an atom’s combining capacity, in terms of electrons gained, lost, or shared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition using either idea.
Award 1 mark for the correct value.

modelAnswer: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom, determined by the number of electrons it gains, loses, or shares.

items.followUp: Differentiate the number of protons and the total number of protons and neutrons in an atom.

rubric.description: Defines atomic number as the number of protons in an atom’s nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying atomic number with the number of protons.

rubric.description: Defines mass number as the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying mass number as the sum of protons and neutrons.

modelAnswer: Atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
Mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.

items.followUp: Define isotopes and name the three isotopes of hydrogen.

rubric.why: Distinguishes isotopes by their atomic and mass numbers.
rubric.description: Defines isotopes as atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the defining similarity and difference.

rubric.why: Gives the number or names of hydrogen’s isotopes.
rubric.description: States that hydrogen has three isotopes: protium, deuterium, and tritium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct number or all three names.

modelAnswer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
Hydrogen has three isotopes: protium, deuterium, and tritium.

items.followUp: Name the isotope commonly used as fuel in nuclear power stations and state how it produces energy.

rubric.why: Identifies an isotope used for nuclear power generation.
rubric.description: Names uranium-235 as a fuel isotope used in nuclear power generation.

rubric.why: Explains how the isotope releases usable energy.
rubric.description: Explains that controlled nuclear fission releases heat, which is used to generate electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking fission or a chain reaction to heat generation.

modelAnswer: Uranium-235 is used as fuel in nuclear power stations.
Controlled nuclear fission releases heat; this heat produces steam that drives turbines to generate electricity.

items.followUp: State how electronegativity changes down a group and across a period.

rubric.why: Gives the periodic trend across a period.
rubric.description: States that electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct trend across a period.

rubric.why: Gives the periodic trend down a group.
rubric.description: States that electronegativity generally decreases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct trend down a group.

modelAnswer: Electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period.
Electronegativity generally decreases down a group.

items.followUp: Describe how shielding effect changes down a group and across a period.

rubric.why: Gives the shielding trend down a group.
rubric.description: States that shielding effect increases down a group as the number of occupied electron shells increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding increases down a group.

rubric.why: Gives the shielding trend across a period.
rubric.description: States that shielding effect remains nearly constant across a period because added electrons enter the same shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding remains nearly constant across a period.

modelAnswer: Shielding effect increases down a group because each successive element has an additional occupied electron shell.
Across a period, shielding effect remains nearly constant because electrons are added to the same shell.

items.followUp: State the basis on which elements are arranged in the modern periodic table.

rubric.description: States that elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct arrangement principle.

rubric.why: Gives the periodic law that underlies the table.
rubric.description: States that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct periodic relationship.

modelAnswer: The modern periodic table is an arrangement of elements in order of increasing atomic number.
In it, the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

items.followUp: Define intramolecular forces and distinguish them from intermolecular forces.

rubric.why: Identifies which particles the forces act between.
rubric.description: Defines intermolecular forces as forces of attraction between molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying attraction between molecules.

rubric.why: Distinguishes intermolecular forces from bonds within molecules.
rubric.description: Notes that intermolecular forces are generally weaker than the chemical bonds within molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct comparison of relative strength.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction between molecules.
They are generally weaker than the chemical bonds within molecules.
